title: Sources manifest
description: sources.yaml at the root of a dataset repo: every file the repo depends on. Hand-edited; download.py fills in fetched_on, sha256 and bytes. See STANDARD.md §2.

format.description: File or API format: stata, spss, sas, csv, parquet, pdf, html, ddi-xml, rda, socrata-json, ...

path.description: Where download.py puts the file, relative to the repo root. Under data/ for anything build-only.

convert.description: How the downloaded file is converted to the file at `path`, with the tool's version, e.g. "pdftotext -layout (poppler 24.02)". sha256 and bytes are then of the converted file, which depends on the converter's version.

documents.description: For documentation and upstream packages: the releases this source documents, e.g. gssrdoc 0.9 documents 7224r3. Can differ from `releases`, the releases it's used to build.

lists_only_occurring_codes.description: For a codebook: true when it lists a code only if the release's data has cases with it (NSFG prints no zero rows). A code missing from such a codebook may still be valid, so comparing releases (pdt diff, link rules) must not read its absence as a dropped code.

version.description: For an upstream package: the release tag or commit it was pinned to.

live.description: true for a source the publisher changes in place (an open-data portal table or its metadata API). sha256 identifies the snapshot the build used; a later mismatch means the source changed, not that the download failed.

acquisition.description: automated: download.py fetches it. manual: a person must fetch it (login, click-through, blocked client); manual_steps says how.
